enunciado: Which phrase names the source of information?
explicacion: According to / Apparently introduce the source. So basically / Overall / In short sum up.

enunciado: Report: “The tablets ease the pain within an hour.”
opciones: She said that the tablets eased the pain within an hour.
She said me that the tablets ease the pain.
She told that the tablets eased the pain.
She said to the tablets eased the pain.
explicacion: Say (that) + clause, usually one tense back. Tell needs a person: She told me that…

enunciado: “I'll send a follow-up email.” → She said she ___ a follow-up email.
explicacion: Will becomes would in reported speech.

enunciado: Which word reports something you heard, without naming the source?
explicacion: Apparently, the delivery was delayed (I heard this from someone).

enunciado: Which phrase gives your final conclusion?
opciones: So basically, it sounds like the easier option.
explicacion: So basically / Overall / In short give the main point at the end.

enunciado: “Did they say when exactly?” is used to…
explicacion: Clarifying questions check details: Did they say when exactly? Was it confirmed?
